newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end mixed but spreads to U.S. narrow.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end mixed but spreads to U.S. narrow.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed on Wednesday, hurt by strong U.S. economic data, but outperformed U.S. Treasuries amid recent strength in the Canadian dollar, analysts said.

"The (U.S.) durable goods report was pretty robust," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs. "It raises the odds of another Fed move coming in May. That's really what hurt the U.S. bond market and by extension our market, which outperformed a little bit."
Canada's 30,-year benchmark bond traded flat at C$109.10 to yield 7.22 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.99 percent. The spread between the two narrowed to 23 basis points from 24 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
Canadian and U.S. bonds weakened this morning after U.S. durable goods orders for February rose a stronger than expected 1.5 percent. Goods had been forecast to fall.

Analysts said the impact on Canadian bonds was cushioned by a strong performance in the Canadian dollar overnight. Tuesday's U.S. interest rate hike had been widely expected to weaken the Canadian currency.

"I think the Canadian dollar held in very nicely. Pretty well everyone is watching that. It actually strengthened overnight so that allowed the Canadian bond market to outperform," said Philip Strathy, vice-president of Strathy Investments Ltd.
In economic news, Statistics Canada this morning reported that the industrial product price index rose 0.1 percent in February from January and was flat from a year earlier.
In new issue news, the Province of Ontario on Wednesday set C$500 million of 7.6 percent bonds due June 2, 2027 in financial markets, said lead manager Nesbitt Burns.
The bond was priced at C$101.607 to yield 7.46 percent, 24 basis points over the Government of Canada's 8.0 percent bond due June 1, 2023.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.13 to C$102.83 to yield 6.598. The U.S. bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.78 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 18 basis points from 14 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.15 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.34 percent.
